name: What happens to the concrete and debris after pool demolition?

mainEntity.name: Is pool debris recycled, hauled to landfill, or reused as fill material?
mainEntity.text: Is pool debris recycled, hauled to landfill, or reused as fill material?

acceptedAnswer.text: After demolition, the concrete shell, rebar, tile, and other debris usually get sorted, hauled away, and taken to licensed disposal or recycling facilities. In some cases, concrete can be recycled, but not every site or contractor handles material the same way. Some crews may use select clean material on-site, while others remove nearly everything. Homeowners should ask where the debris goes, whether recycling is part of the contractor’s process, and whether hauling is included in the base price. Disposal costs can be significant, especially for larger pools or difficult-access properties. A transparent contractor should be able to explain the debris plan clearly before work begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool debris is typically broken up, hauled away, and disposed of at licensed facilities, and some concrete may be recycled if local facilities accept it. Homeowners should confirm whether disposal and hauling are included in the quote.
